dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: The proposition asserting the existence of a universal positive real constant c such that every finite nonempty independent family of standard real Gaussian random variables has an integrable pointwise maximum whose expectation is at least c times sqrt(log N).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: This is the entire target proposition.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a sequence X and natural number N, this is the pointwise supremum of X_i over i in Fin N when N>0, and the constant-zero function when N=0.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Under the explicit hypothesis N>0, it is exactly the random variable ω ↦ max_{0≤i<N} X_i(ω); its zero branch is unreachable.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: The real Gaussian probability measure with mean 0 and nonnegative parameter 1, hence the standard Gaussian law under the library's Gaussian parameter convention.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Every X_i is required to have this same standard Gaussian law.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a nonempty finite index type, it takes the supremum of a family of real-valued functions; because the function-space supremum is pointwise, its value at ω is the maximum of the finitely many values X_i(ω).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the finite pointwise maximum used by LocalDef002.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: A positive natural number N makes Fin N nonempty.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It provides the nonemptiness required to form the nonempty finite supremum in LocalDef002.

dependency_coverage.name: And
dependency_coverage.meaning: Logical conjunction.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It joins c>0 to the universal assertion and, inside that assertion, joins integrability to the expectation lower bound.

dependency_coverage.name: Exists
dependency_coverage.meaning: Existential quantification.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It asserts that one real constant c can be chosen before, and uniformly for, all subsequent probability spaces, families, and N.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin
dependency_coverage.meaning: Fin N is the finite type of natural indices i satisfying i<N.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It indexes precisely the first N random variables.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin.val
dependency_coverage.meaning: It extracts the underlying natural number from an element of Fin N.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It turns a finite index i into the sequence index used in X i.val.

dependency_coverage.name: HMul.hMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: Heterogeneous multiplication supplied by an HMul instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For reals here, it forms the ordinary product c·sqrt(log N).

dependency_coverage.name: InnerProductSpace.toNormedSpace
dependency_coverage.meaning: It derives a normed-space structure from an inner-product-space structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is typeclass infrastructure enabling the real-valued Bochner integral and does not add a mathematical hypothesis.

dependency_coverage.name: LE.le
dependency_coverage.meaning: The less-than-or-equal relation supplied by an LE instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It expresses the real lower bound c·sqrt(log N) ≤ ∫ max_i X_i dμ.

dependency_coverage.name: LT.lt
dependency_coverage.meaning: The strict-order relation supplied by an LT instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It expresses both positivity of c and positivity of N using the usual orders on Real and Nat.

dependency_coverage.name: Measurable

binders: There exists a real number c.
Universally quantify over an arbitrary type Ω equipped with a measurable-space structure.
Universally quantify over a measure μ on Ω, together with an instance asserting that μ is a probability measure.
Universally quantify over a sequence X : Nat → Ω → Real of real-valued functions.
Universally quantify over a natural number N.
hypotheses: For every i in Fin N, the random variable X_{i.val} is measurable.
For every i in Fin N, X_{i.val} has law gaussianReal 0 1 under μ, i.e. the standard real Gaussian law.
The family i ↦ X_{i.val}, indexed by Fin N, is mutually independent under μ.
conclusions: The pointwise maximum ω ↦ max_{i in Fin N} X_{i.val}(ω) is integrable with respect to μ.
Its expectation satisfies c·sqrt(log(real(N))) ≤ ∫_Ω max_{i in Fin N} X_{i.val}(ω) dμ(ω).
mathematical_definitions: For N>0, LocalDef002 X N is the pointwise finite maximum max_{0≤i<N} X_i; for N=0 it is defined to be identically zero.
LocalDef003 is gaussianReal 0 1, the standard real Gaussian probability measure.
The integral of the real-valued maximum under the probability measure μ is its expectation.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There is a universal positive real constant c such that, for every probability space and every positive integer N, if X_0,...,X_{N-1} are measurable, mutually independent real random variables and each has the standard Gaussian law, then their pointwise maximum is integrable and its expected value is at least c sqrt(log N).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The statement concerns only positive N. The N=0 branch of LocalDef002, where the maximum is defined as zero, is never used under the hypotheses.
The constant c is chosen before Ω, μ, X, and N, so it is uniform over all probability spaces, all such Gaussian families, and all positive N.
For N=1, log N=0, so the numerical lower bound reduces to 0≤E[X_0]; for a centered standard Gaussian this is equality, making that case noninformative about the size of c.
The proposition assumes both componentwise measurability and HasLaw conditions; it does not merely quantify arbitrary functions with a distribution informally assigned to them.
Independence is asserted only for the first N members indexed by Fin N; values X_i for i≥N are unrestricted and irrelevant.
The conclusion uses the pointwise finite maximum, not the maximum of absolute values and not the supremum of an infinite sequence.
No upper bound, asymptotic equivalence, optimal value of c, or dependence of the expectation on N beyond the stated lower bound is encoded.
No atomlessness, completeness, standard-Borel condition, or other structural property of Ω is required beyond a measurable space and a probability measure.

Because the hypotheses include existence of a fully independent standard-Gaussian family on the chosen space, the implication is vacuous for choices of Ω and μ on which no such X exists; nevertheless the universal statement constrains every family satisfying the hypotheses.
Integrability is part of the conclusion rather than an assumption.
ambiguities: The dependency presents gaussianReal's second argument as an NNReal parameter and its body through gaussianPDF, but does not explicitly label that parameter as variance or standard deviation. At the value 1, both conventions yield the standard Gaussian, so this does not change the translated target.
The phrase 'expectation' is an interpretation of the displayed Bochner integral under a probability measure; the formal target itself uses MeasureTheory.integral.
The numerical constant c is existentially asserted but neither named, optimized, nor given an explicit value.
